# `Q-10-7` — Invalid Pipe Arguments

> A template pipe received arguments it cannot accept.

## What this means

Several template pipes take arguments — `$x/left 10$` needs a
width, `$x/alpha$` needs its input to be a positive integer,
and so on. This error fires when the pipe's arguments (or the
input value) are not of the shape the pipe needs. The
template's strict-mode setting determines whether the
diagnostic is a warning or an error; the value passes through
unchanged.

## Why this happens

Common causes:

- **A width pipe given a non-integer width**
  (`$x/left "ten"$`).
- **An `alpha:` or `roman:` pipe given a non-positive-integer
  value** (`$x/alpha$` where `x` is a string).
- **Too few or too many arguments** for the pipe's signature.

## How to fix

Check the pipe's expected arguments against the Pandoc template
documentation. If the input is the problem, transform the value
upstream (or set it with a sensible default) so the pipe
receives what it expects.

## Related
